text: [on paper] $J_k=\mathrm{span}\{\mu(r)-1\}+J_{k-1}a+aJ_{k-1}$ (Lemma N1): one Howell form per level, no closure rounds. A word whose prefix or suffix is not a standard monomial of the previous level is rewritten by a fixed rule into later columns (a projection $\pi_k$ with kernel in $J_k$), so only the candidates $C_k$ stay as columns; the generators of $\pi_k(J_k)$ are the relators, both shifts of the torsion rows, and few "overlaps" (Lemma N2).

text: Columns in increasing degree, as everywhere in B. Facts used [on paper, §3.4]: the Howell form of $J_n$ truncated to degrees $<k$ is a Howell form of $J_k$; the columns without a unit pivot (the standard monomials $S_k$) are closed under prefixes and suffixes (if $u$ has a unit pivot, $u-\mathrm{NF}(u)\in J$ with $\mathrm{NF}(u)$ on later columns, and multiplying by $a_j$ on either side keeps "later"); $\mathrm{NF}_k(u)$ lies in the standard monomials of degree $\ge\deg u$. The number of standard monomials is at least $\dim_{\mathbb F_2}\Delta_{\mathbb F_2}/\Delta^n_{\mathbb F_2}$ (generators, Jennings, §6.4), a lower bound for every monomial basis.
